assets.alt: Hand-drawn skyline of Cairo's New Administrative Capital: a slender central tower flanked by blocky high-rises, black line with red pencil overlay.
assets.caption: Figure 1 — the skyline of the New Administrative Capital.

assets.alt: Perspective sketch of the New Administrative Capital's grand entrance: colonnaded blocks flank a wide axis with a tower behind, red pencil over black line.
assets.caption: Figure 2 — the grand entrance of the New Administrative Capital.

assets.alt: Sketch of a monumental New Administrative Capital building: a heavy roof slab over tall pylons, flanked by gridded office blocks, red pencil over black line.
assets.caption: Figure 3 — the building shape and size outline.

assets.alt: Freehand sketch of a corner building in West el Balad, Cairo: rounded turret with dome, tiered balconies and arched shopfronts, red pencil over black line.
assets.caption: Figure 4 — façade of a typical building in West el Balad.

assets.alt: Worm's-eye sketch of a curved bay-fronted apartment block in West el Balad, Cairo, its balconies and shop awning picked out in red pencil over black line.
assets.caption: Figure 5 — emphasis on balcony and street shading in West el Balad.

assets.alt: Sketch of a Zamalek apartment building's upper storeys: rounded corner bay, cornices, balconies and ground-floor arcade, red pencil over black line.
assets.caption: Figure 6 — typical exterior of a building in Zamalek.

assets.alt: Freehand sketch looking up between two Zamalek buildings: windows either side and a red-pencil shading structure spanning the narrow street.
assets.caption: Figure 7 (upper) — worm's-eye view in the narrow streets between buildings, Zamalek.

assets.alt: Freehand sketch of balconies and shaded bays stepping along a narrow gap between Zamalek buildings, balustrades picked out in red pencil.
assets.caption: Figure 7 (lower) — balconies and shading in Zamalek.

assets.alt: Freehand panoramic sketch of a Cairo Ashwa’iyat: dense informal rooftops, a minaret and taller blocks, with rooftop structures picked out in red pencil.
assets.caption: Figure 8 — Ashwa’iyat landscape overview.

assets.alt: Street-level sketch of Ashwa’iyat apartment blocks in Cairo, a tall tower and neighbouring slabs, windows and balconies marked over in red pencil.
assets.caption: Figure 9 — street view of a typical Ashwa’iyat façade.

assets.alt: Freehand sketch of a half-built Cairo apartment block: concrete frame, open stairs, brick infill and rebar, with red pencil marking unfinished construction.
assets.caption: Figure 11 — a semi-inhabited, broken-down Ashwaya (singular of Ashwa’iyat).

assets.alt: Dusk render of a circular two-storey music hall with a wide ring roof, glazed façades and figures on stepped terraces beside a reflecting pool.
assets.caption: External perspective of the Music Institution at dusk: the circular performance hall above a stepped landscape descending towards the water.

assets.alt: Exploded isometric sketch of a circular music building: a ring of rooms around a central void above a performance hall with curved raked seating.

assets.alt: Hand-drawn flowing parallel lines like a curved musical stave, with a pair of quavers.
assets.caption: Concept board motif: flowing lines translate the movement of the canal into the paths through the building.

assets.alt: Site plan of the Music Institution, Reading: a circular building among trees, with curved stepped terraces descending to a canal crossing the site diagonally.
assets.caption: Site plan: the circular hall set within a stepped landscape of terraces and trees descending to the canal edge. No scale is stated in the source.

assets.alt: Site analysis collage: hand-drawn street plan with the site in red, graffiti walls, black-and-white weir photographs and people walking beside the canal.
assets.caption: Site analysis collage, layering a hand-drawn plan of the canal-side site with the graffiti, weirs and movement of people found along the water.
assets.rightsNote: The photographs within the collage are site documentation whose authorship is not stated in the portfolio.

assets.alt: Section through the Music Institution: recording studios, the double-height performance space with stepped seating, café and mezzanine under a green roof, with outdoor stepped seating descending to the right; construction and space-use legends at the margins.
assets.caption: Section: a continuous sequence links practice, performance and the public landscape. Legends CT01–CT20 (construction) and SU01– (space use) are part of the drawing.

assets.alt: Exploded axonometric of the Music Institution: ground ring with the performance hall, upper ring with practice rooms, and the roof disc with its skylight, above the landscaped site with curved stepped seating; space-use legend SU01–SU14.
assets.caption: Exploded axonometric: ground floor, upper floor and roof garden lifted apart over the stepped landscape (legend SU01–SU14).

assets.alt: Section 1:50 through Maison Peplum: two floors inside the existing warehouse shell with a timber stair, curved timber fins rising on both faces and over the pitched roof, the canal at left, and ground build-up labels below.
assets.caption: Section at 1:50: two floors within the retained shell, fins on both faces and over the roof, the canal to one side.
